_comment: Committed format-version-1 (framed stream) vectors. Generated once, deliberately, by gen_vectors_test.go -write-framed-vectors, each with a fixed DEK and a fixed salt so the ciphertext is reproducible; see docs/format.md, 'Test vectors'. TestVectors_MatchCommittedTestdata decrypts each entry's ciphertext_hex directly. It must never be replaced by re-encrypting plaintext_hex and comparing, since the whole point is to catch a silent wire-format change that a round trip cannot. If a committed ciphertext stops decrypting, that is a real failure, not a vector to refresh. More than one vector is committed deliberately: a single small vector whose only frame is index 0 with final=true cannot distinguish several wire format changes (nonce/AAD index endianness, final-flag encoding, wire stride, the finality rule) from the correct format, because index 0 is all-zeros and final=true is the only branch it exercises. These bytes are NOT the ones cas/internal/crypto wrote. The magic and the HKDF info string were renamed from CASF1 to SEAL1 when the format was extracted, which changes both the frame key and every tag, so CAS's ciphertext does not decrypt here and this fixture was regenerated once for that rename. The DEKs, salts, frame sizes, tenant and content addresses are CAS's fixture unchanged, so the diff that regenerated this file shows the format changing and little else; the only other change is the first vector's plaintext, an ASCII sentence that used to name CAS. salt_hex and frame_size are recorded only so the fixture's provenance is auditable; the decoder reads both from the header, as every real reader does.
